lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Job: overview
nodes.d: Job opens with a righteous man losing everything (1-2), moves through his lament and long exchanges with three friends (3-31), Elihu (32-37) and the LORD answering from the whirlwind (38-41), and ends with Job’s repentance and restoration (42).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Job in four or five parts and name who speaks in each?
ev: Outline the book of Job in its main parts: prologue, speeches, the LORD’s answer, epilogue.

nodes.t: Job’s integrity and the loss of everything
nodes.d: Job is described as blameless and God-fearing and is very rich; the LORD allows Satan to take his possessions and children, and Job worships, saying the LORD gave and the LORD has taken away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Job in chapter 1 and what he said when he heard the news?
ev: Retell what Job lost in chapter 1 and how he responded (1:20-22).

nodes.t: Job’s sores and his friends’ silence
nodes.d: Satan is allowed to strike Job’s body with sore boils, his wife tells him to curse God and die, Job refuses, and three friends come and sit with him seven days without speaking.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Job says to his wife and what his three friends do when they arrive?
ev: Explain how Job answers his wife in 2:9-10 and what the three friends do in 2:11-13.

nodes.t: Job laments the day of his birth
nodes.d: Job breaks the silence by cursing the day he was born and asking why light is given to those in misery who long for death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks in chapter 3 and how it differs from his words in chapters 1-2?
ev: Summarize Job’s complaint in chapter 3 and name what he wishes had happened (3:11-13).

nodes.t: Eliphaz’s first speech
nodes.d: Eliphaz says the innocent do not perish and those who sow wickedness reap it, tells of a night vision asking whether mortal man can be more just than God, and urges Job to seek God and not despise his correction.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state Eliphaz’s main argument to Job in chapters 4-5?
ev: Identify Eliphaz’s argument in 4:7-8 and his advice in 5:8 and 5:17.

nodes.t: Job answers: my grief is heavy, my friends fail me
nodes.d: Job says his grief outweighs the sand of the sea, compares his friends to a stream that fails in summer, and cries that his days are hopeless and short, asking God why he is watched so closely.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Job answers Eliphaz in chapters 6-7 and what he asks of God?
ev: Find the image Job uses for his friends in 6:15-20.
Describe how Job speaks to God in 7:11-21.

nodes.t: Bildad’s first speech
nodes.d: Bildad asks whether God perverts justice, suggests Job’s children sinned, and says that if Job is pure God will restore him while the hope of the godless perishes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Bildad says about God’s justice and what he thinks it means for Job?
ev: Note Bildad’s questions in 8:3 and the promise in 8:20-21.

nodes.t: How can a man be right with God? Job longs for a mediator
nodes.d: Job agrees that a man cannot contend with a God of great power, laments that there is no daysman between them to lay a hand on both, and in chapter 10 pleads with God to show why he contends with him, recalling that God made him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Job means by wanting a daysman in 9:33?
ev: Find Job’s question in 9:2 and his wish in 9:33.
List what Job says about being made by God in 10:8-12.

nodes.t: Zophar’s first speech
nodes.d: Zophar accuses Job of empty talk, says God’s wisdom cannot be searched out, and promises that if Job puts away iniquity and prepares his heart he will be secure, while the eyes of the wicked fail.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize Zophar’s first speech and compare it with Bildad’s?
ev: What does Zophar say about searching out God (11:7-9) and about repentance (11:13-19)?

nodes.t: Job replies: God’s power, and whether a man will live again
nodes.d: Job tells the friends he is not inferior to them, says wisdom and strength belong to God, who overturns counsellors and kings, declares he will trust God though he slay him, and in chapter 14 asks whether a man who dies shall live again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Job speaks of God’s power in chapter 12 and what he asks about death in 14:14?
ev: Locate 13:15 and 14:14 and say what each expresses.
List things God does to rulers in 12:17-21.

nodes.t: Eliphaz’s second speech: the wicked man’s torment
nodes.d: Eliphaz rebukes Job for vain words and describes at length how the wicked man suffers pain and fear all his days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Eliphaz accuses Job of in chapter 15 and how he describes the wicked?
ev: Describe the picture of the wicked man in 15:20-35.

nodes.t: Job: miserable comforters, and a witness on high
nodes.d: Job calls his friends miserable comforters, says God has broken and worn him down, yet declares that his prayer is pure and that his witness is in heaven; his spirit is broken and the grave is ready for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Job describes his friends and what he says about a witness in chapters 16-17?
ev: Find the phrase Job uses for his friends in 16:2 and what he claims in 16:17-19.

nodes.t: Bildad’s second speech: the light of the wicked is put out
nodes.d: Bildad describes the wicked man snared, terrified and rooted out of his tent so that his remembrance perishes from the earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list two of the pictures Bildad uses for the end of the wicked?
ev: List the images of the wicked man’s end in chapter 18.

nodes.t: I know that my redeemer lives
nodes.d: Job says God has fenced his way and his family and friends have forsaken him, and he longs for his words to be written, declaring that he knows his redeemer lives and that in his flesh he shall see God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Job 19:25-27 and say what Job expects in spite of his condition?
ev: Read 19:23-27 and state what Job says he knows and expects to see.
List the losses Job names in 19:13-20.

nodes.t: Zophar’s second speech: the triumph of the wicked is short
nodes.d: Zophar says the triumphing of the wicked is short, that ill-gotten riches will be vomited up, and that God casts the fury of his wrath on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Zophar’s claim about the wicked in chapter 20?
ev: State Zophar’s claim in 20:5 and the portion he assigns the wicked in 20:29.

nodes.t: Job: the wicked often prosper
nodes.d: Job answers that the wicked live, grow old, see their children established and die at ease, and asks how often the lamp of the wicked is put out, rejecting his friends’ consolations as falsehood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Job’s words in chapter 21 challenge the friends’ view of the wicked?
ev: Find where Job describes the wicked at ease in 21:7-13 and contrast it with the friends’ claims.

nodes.t: Eliphaz’s third speech: accusation and a call to return
nodes.d: Eliphaz asks whether a man can profit God, accuses Job of specific wrongs against the poor, and calls him to return to the Almighty and be built up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Eliphaz now accuses Job of and what he tells him to do?
ev: List the charges Eliphaz makes in 22:5-9 and the invitation in 22:21-30.

nodes.t: Job: I cannot find him, yet he knows my way
nodes.d: Job longs to come to God’s seat and plead his case but cannot find him forward or backward; he says God knows the way he takes and that when tried he shall come forth as gold, and chapter 24 asks why the oppression of the poor goes unpunished.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Job wants from God in chapter 23 and what troubles him in chapter 24?
ev: Find 23:3-10 and say what Job wants and what he is confident of in 23:10.

nodes.t: Bildad’s short speech and Job’s reply
nodes.d: Bildad says dominion and fear are with God and asks how man can be clean before him; Job replies by describing God’s power over the deep and the heavens and swears he will hold fast his integrity until he dies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Job vows in chapter 27 and why he refuses to agree with his friends?
ev: Compare the length of Bildad’s speech (ch. 25) with Job’s answers (26-27).
Find Job’s vow in 27:2-6.

nodes.t: Where shall wisdom be found?
nodes.d: Job describes how men mine silver and gold from the earth, yet wisdom cannot be found in the deep or bought with gold; God alone knows its place, and tells man that the fear of the LORD is wisdom and to depart from evil is understanding.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Job 28:28 and explain how it answers the question asked in 28:12 and 28:20?
ev: Contrast what men can find by mining (28:1-11) with what they cannot (28:12-22).
State the answer in 28:28.

nodes.t: Job remembers his former honour and describes his shame
nodes.d: Job recalls the months when God preserved him, when he was honoured and delivered the poor, then describes being mocked by those younger, with God not hearing his cry.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Job’s condition in chapter 29 with his condition in chapter 30?
ev: Contrast Job’s life in chapter 29 with chapter 30.

nodes.t: Job’s oath of innocence
nodes.d: Job lists wrongs he says he has not done, from lust and falsehood to neglecting the poor, the fatherless and the stranger, trusting gold, and rejoicing at an enemy’s fall, and desires that the Almighty answer him; the words of Job end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of wrong Job says he has avoided in chapter 31?
ev: Choose three of Job’s denials in chapter 31 and say which commands of right conduct each shows.

nodes.t: Elihu speaks: anger at Job and the three
nodes.d: The three men stop answering because Job is righteous in his own eyes; Elihu, younger than they, is angry with Job for justifying himself and with the friends for finding no answer, and says the Spirit within man gives understanding.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Elihu speaks and why he waited?
ev: Name why Elihu was angry with Job and with the three friends (32:2-3).

nodes.t: Elihu: God speaks, and sends an interpreter
nodes.d: Elihu says God speaks to man in dreams and by suffering to turn him from pride, and that if there is a messenger, an interpreter, to show man his uprightness, God is gracious and ransoms him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list two ways Elihu says God speaks to men in chapter 33?
ev: Find 33:14-30 and list the ways Elihu says God speaks to and restores a person.

nodes.t: Elihu: God does no wickedness
nodes.d: Elihu says God will not do wickedly or pervert judgment and rewards each man according to his work, rebukes Job for saying it profits nothing to delight in God, and says God sees but does not owe man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state what Elihu says about God’s justice in chapter 34?
ev: Find the sentence in 34:10 and the charge against Job in 34:35-37.

nodes.t: Elihu: the greatness of God in the storm
nodes.d: Elihu says God is mighty, teaches through affliction, and is beyond understanding; he describes God’s command over rain, lightning and thunder and tells Job to stand still and consider God’s wondrous works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three works of God Elihu points to in chapters 36-37?
ev: List the weather phenomena Elihu names in 36:27-37:13.

nodes.t: The LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind: creation and the animals
nodes.d: The LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind with questions about the foundations of the earth, the sea, light, rain, the stars, and the lion, raven, wild goat, wild ass, ostrich, horse and hawk, none of which Job made or controls.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD is showing Job by asking questions about creation in chapters 38-39?
ev: Pick five of the LORD’s questions in chapter 38 and say what each says about God’s power.
List the animals in chapter 39.

nodes.t: Job lays his hand on his mouth
nodes.d: The LORD asks whether the faultfinder will instruct the Almighty and challenges Job to answer; Job says he is vile and will not answer again, and the LORD calls him to gird up his loins and asks whether he will condemn God to justify himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Job responds in 40:3-5 and what the LORD asks next?
ev: Compare Job’s first reply (40:3-5) with the LORD’s second challenge (40:6-14).

nodes.t: Behemoth and Leviathan
nodes.d: The LORD describes behemoth, which he made, as chief of his ways with great strength, and leviathan, which no man can hook, tame or stand before; he asks who can stand before him and says all under heaven is his.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD speaks of behemoth and leviathan to Job?
ev: Name what the LORD says in 41:10-11 about standing before the creature and before him.

nodes.t: Job sees God and repents
nodes.d: Job says he knows God can do everything, that he spoke of things too wonderful for him, that he had heard of God by the ear but now his eye sees him, and he abhors himself and repents in dust and ashes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Job 42:1-6 and describe what Job confesses?
ev: Say what Job confesses in 42:2-6 and what changed for him from hearing to seeing.

nodes.t: The LORD restores Job and rebukes the friends
nodes.d: The LORD says the three friends have not spoken of him rightly as Job has, tells them to offer a burnt offering with Job praying for them, and then gives Job twice as much as before, seven sons and three daughters, and many more years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells the friends to do, and what happens to Job at the end?
ev: State why the LORD is angry with Eliphaz and his friends (42:7).
List what the LORD gives Job in 42:10-16.

nodes.t: 1 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: Servants, builders and God's temple
nodes.d: Paul tells the divided Corinthians that he and Apollos are only servants, that God gives the increase, that Jesus Christ is the one foundation, and that the church is God's temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who gives growth in the church and what the foundation is, using 1 Corinthians 3?
ev: Explain the picture of planting and watering (3:6-7)
Say what the one foundation is (3:11)
Explain what happens to each builder's work (3:12-15)
Say why the church is called God's temple (3:16-17)

nodes.t: James: overview
nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.t: Patience until the coming of the Lord
nodes.d: James urges patience like the farmer waiting for rain, points to the prophets and Job as examples, says the Lord is pitiful and merciful, and tells them not to swear oaths.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to be patient until the coming of the Lord?
ev: Describe the farmer picture of patience
Name the examples of endurance James gives
Say what James tells them about oaths
